newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsica suspect held for machinegunning police.
newsitem.headline: Corsica suspect held for machinegunning police.

text.p: Judicial authorities have placed a 25-year-old Corsican under investigation on suspicion of machinegunning a police station last month, justice sources said on Sunday.

Jean-Francois Mariotti, one of three brothers seized at their home by an elite unit of the paramilitary gendarmerie police on Friday, was ordered held in preventive custody in the island capital Ajaccio.
His two brothers were released without charge. The gendarmes had used explosives to burst into a house in the village of Urbalacone south of Ajaccio and detain the three men.
Mariotti is suspected of taking part in the attack on the Sainte Marie Sicche gendarmerie barracks on December 27. A gendarme had returned fire but apparently without hitting the attackers' car.
Investigators said the suspects were not believed to be linked to separatists who have recently stepped up their 20-year-campaign for greater autonomy from mainland France.

Corsica has been trying to shake off a reputation for lawlessness -- murder rates are far higher than on the mainland. In 1996, there were 22 killings on the island of 250,000 people, down from 40 in 1995.
